messages:
incident-bot: Paging alice (oncall) — GPU pool exhausted in us-west-2, autoscale failing, multiple customer requests throttled. Severity: P1.

alice (oncall): on it. seeing lots of 429s from /v1/generate, and GPU queue length spiking. thanks for the page. will gather quick facts.

ben (sre): summary from dashboards: GPU utilization at 99%, inference-request-queue length ~12k, HPA for gpu-deployment shows 0 metric data for external/gpu_queue_length for last 5m. prometheus scrape for metrics-adapter looks flaky.

carla (runtime): this smells like metrics-adapter -> HPA pipeline. if the metrics adapter isn't receiving Prometheus, HPA won't scale. can someone check metrics-adapter logs?

dan (eng-infra): running: kubectl -n infra logs deploy/metrics-adapter --tail=200
```
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/metrics-adapter --tail=200
```
logs show repeated: "error scraping prometheus: context deadline exceeded" and a spike of 503s to prometheus-query.

alice (oncall): @dan any alerts on prometheus?

dan (eng-infra): prometheus cluster is healthy, but there's a CPU balloon on prom-query pods; queries are timing out under heavy cardinality. I see elevated selector cardinality from gpu_exporter job.

autoscale-bot: HPA gpu-worker-hpa has not received external metric samples for 7m; current replicas: 8; desired: Unknown.

carla (runtime): queue growth is real — workers are busy, batch sizes are large, and fallback to CPU is disabled. customers hitting latency and 429s.

eve (support): getting inbound tickets from 3 customers in the finance sandbox region reporting errors and timeouts. posting customer IDs to the incident doc.

alice (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) manually scale GPU pool up to buy time 2) reduce batch sizes to lower latency 3) restart metrics-adapter to recover metrics pipeline 4) if prometheus query latency persists, fallback HPA to 'pods' or apply manual replica patch 5) communicate to customers. executing now.

ben (sre): manual scale command: `kubectl -n prod scale deployment gpu-worker --replicas=24` — going to apply, but watch for capacity on the infra side (quota).

dan (eng-infra): increased cluster GPU quota via autoscaler toggle and added 8 nodes. Infra reports additional nodes provisioning (AWS ASG). ETA ~3m.

alice (oncall): scaled gpu-worker to 24 (manual). monitoring queue — still climbing but growth rate slowed.

carla (runtime): lowering batch size via feature flag: `INFER_BATCH_MAX=8` rolled to 30% of traffic for now to reduce tail latency.

ben (sre): restarting metrics-adapter now: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/metrics-adapter`

dan (eng-infra): note: prometheus-query pods still show high CPU. I'm going to temporarily reduce scrape cardinality by excluding per-request labels for gpu_exporter in scrapes to reduce query fanout. patching prometheus config.

alice (oncall): patch applied to prometheus scrape relabel: removing "request_id" label for gpu metrics. restarting scrapers.

autoscale-bot: metrics-adapter: connected to prometheus. external metrics flow resuming.

ben (sre): HPA reports new metric samples. HPA desired replicas estimated ~20, but external controller still reconciling.

carla (runtime): queue length now trending down from 12k -> 4.2k over 10m. customer errors decreasing.

eve (support): customers reporting fewer 429s, one customer still seeing intermittent timeouts. CS has sent an interim status update.

alice (oncall): Observed root cause (preliminary): Prometheus query latency caused metrics-adapter timeouts. Root triggers: sudden spike in cardinality from a recent inference debug exporter that started emitting high-cardinality labels. This overwhelmed query paths used by adapter, leading to no external metrics presented to HPA, so autoscaler could not scale quickly and queue grew until manual scale and infra nodes came up.

dan (eng-infra): mitigation checklist completed: - scaled nodes + GPU capacity added - reduced scrape cardinality - restarted metrics-adapter - temporary manual replica patch to gpu-worker - reduced batch sizes to reduce tail latency

ben (sre): next steps: 1) blacklist the offending debug exporter (we found a canary trace job emitting extra labels) 2) add circuit-breaker/timeout to prometheus queries used by metrics-adapter 3) add synthetic test generating external metric samples to monitor adapter liveness 4) make HPA fallback rule: if external metric absent for >2m, switch to CPU utilization metric or a conservative replica count.

carla (runtime): I'll work on a patch for dynamic batch-scaling and a conservative fallback HPA policy.

alice (oncall): handing off to ben for long-term infra and retro. ben, you're next oncall for post-incident follow-up. leaving a short runbook notes: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/gpu-autoscale-metrics-failure (added incident timeline).

ben (sre): taking handoff. I'll keep monitoring for 60m then start postmortem with owners.

eve (support): I've posted customer impact details and notification copy in the incident channel. customers updated: "We identified a metrics ingestion problem that temporarily prevented automatic scaling; we have increased capacity and are investigating root cause. We'll follow up with timeline and remediation."

alice (oncall): final: severity downgraded to P2. queue back to baseline and 429s ~95% reduced. handing off.

autoscale-bot: Incident closed for oncall alice (oncall) -> handed to ben (sre). Incident duration (active): 40m.

ben (sre): Action items assigned: - dan: add rate-limits and timeouts on prometheus query endpoints - carla: implement HPA fallback policy - dan + infra: add node warm pool and faster GPU node provisioning - alice + docs: update runbook with recent mitigation steps and quick checks for metrics-adapter.

alice (oncall): thanks team. logging follow-up tasks and starting RCA doc now. :thumbsup:
